question.text: GAAR (General Anti-Avoidance Rules) CAN be invoked when a Cat III AIF:

answer.text: Is based in a tax-efficient jurisdiction (alone)
Enters into an impermissible avoidance arrangement whose tax avoidance is NOT sufficiently addressed by an LoB Clause in the DTAA

explanation.text: The Logic: GAAR may be invoked for an impermissible avoidance arrangement. It shall NOT be invoked merely because an entity is in a tax-efficient jurisdiction, or where the tax avoidance is sufficiently addressed by a Limitation of Benefits (LoB) clause in the applicable DTAA. The Trap: Location alone or genuine commercial substance do not trigger GAAR; the test is whether the arrangement is impermissible and whether the LoB clause already addresses the avoidance. Note: Source: NISM-Series-XIX-B AIF (Cat III) Distributors workbook, pp.321-322; see also CBDT Circular No. 7 of 2017.
